assessmentSettings.busybeeScoringInstructions: BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit.

questions.prompt: Use your systematic investigation to identify the variable with the clearest effect on performance. Cite at least three controlled trials and explain the trend and one tradeoff in current, torque, speed, mass, heat, or resource cost.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Evidence must cite at least three systematic trials that isolate a variable. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2.
a. Full credit: Identifies a variable, cites three accurate controlled trials, explains the performance trend, and identifies a supported tradeoff. Partial credit: Gives a reasonable trend with incomplete control or data. No credit: Attributes a change to one variable when several changed or provides no usable evidence.

questions.prompt: Write a claim-evidence-reasoning conclusion defending your optimized motor against the baseline. Cite the complete settings and performance values for both designs, calculate or report the improvement, and explain how magnetic torque, back EMF, friction or load, and the resource/current constraints shaped the redesign.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Grade the baseline-to-optimized comparison, quantitative improvement, motor-physics reasoning, and constraint tradeoff. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3.
a. Full credit: Gives complete baseline and optimized evidence, a correct improvement comparison, explains the important motor relationships, and justifies a constraint-based tradeoff. Partial credit: Gives a supported improvement but incomplete settings, physics, or constraints. No credit: Provides no baseline comparison or unsupported optimization claims.
